body:
meredith@shadow.net (William R. Meredith) wrote:
:
: First of all no one appoint Ted to lead a girl scout troop led along a
: nation. He is just a sociopath with a high IQ and one who by his own
: statement had no moral values.

Who cares if someone is appointed?  Do you think that just because you
vote for somebody it makes them intelligent and able to solve problems?

In this world of hypocrisy, coercion, and lies, those who claim to be
moral are often the most corrupt.  We have to do what we think is right
and disregard the values others try to force on us.

: Wars are fought between nations, Ted is a citizen of the US, who took
: a delight in killing his fellow citizens for reasons that seem more of a
: outgrowth of his sick mind then for any logic reason. He kill for nineteen
: years without trying to tell anyone why!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Wars are also fought within nations.  
- US Civil war
- War on drugs (though over 40 million people have used drugs labeled as
  'illegal' or politically incorrect)

Because the latter is a war of social ideology, there is no reason to not
include other attempts to change social ideology as forms of war.

: I frankly don't think he have any more reason for being a serial killer
: then any other such killer.

Often people are killed in war.  I'm not sure what you're getting at though.

: Sorry if I wish a change in society, I would try to talk my fellow
: citizens into the need for those changes, not kill them for nineteen years
: and then say by the way the reason I been killing you is that I don't agree
: with your technology!

It's not clear that you understand why this isn't possible.  No one has
time anymore for social changes.  We work 40+ hours a week and on top
of that have to waste more time on the system by fixing problems it creates
and doesn't care about, laying the burden on us and consuming our time
(e.g. forcing us to contact the company about incorrect bills and other 
computer errors).  If you're married than you typically spend more time 
with your spouse than chasing down the evils of this world.  If you have
children then you spend time with them instead of organizing campaigns
against the world's problems.  No one wants to hear anything about more
problems outside of their personal ones they're already working on.  That's
part of the reason we've had such mediocre presidents lately - no one
cares, so they'll vote for the guy who seems least harmful to the
nation.  It doesn't matter if they just add to the problems our country
has, as long as they can tell us with a straight face that everything is ok
and they're working to make things even better.

: Why should anyone assume that he is anything but a run of a mill serial
: killer?

Because FC killed for a cause.  Please read the Manifesto and critique it
using words other than "insane" and "ramble".  Use some logical and
descriptive methods to explain the reason you think any part of it is
in error.  That's a conversation that some people might find useful.
Your name-calling and bogus labeling doesn't contribute anything.

: No I don't have to admit that we are losing any freedoms as we surely are
: not as a matter of fact.

Do you know someone can get your SSN, credit history, medical history, and
buying patterns for $50-100?  That's because computers have been abused
to collect data.  And when that data is wrong and you are either denied
credit for an incorrect credit blemish, it is your fault for not checking
the incorrect data that companies have on you.  And when you're denied
medical insurance because of incorrect data (which is much more difficult
to have corrected), you're at the mercy of the maintainers of that data.

We had much more freedom a hundred or two hundred years ago when our
purchases were not tracked in a database and only our personal
doctors knew our medical history.  No one was selling our credit or
medical histories then either.

The future offers us the possibility that we will be tracked even more
closely.  For example, our vehicles were an fairly anonymous mode of
transportation ten years ago and we could drive almost anywhere without
anyone keeping record of it, though we were free only to the extent
that we had to be submissive to whatever local laws had been created.

We will soon be tracked in our vehicles:
- by automatic toll booths that have a virtual token payment sent 
  by a "smart card" so that we don't have to stop.  It'll know who
  we are and automatically deduct the amount or bill us later.  That
  information will sit in a database and will no doubt be analyzed
  and sold (Joe Blow tends to pass through at 9am and come back at 6pm,
  analysis: working stiff)

- technology is also being developed for checking for traffic and
  finding the best routes of travel.  This is done by having a system
  measure traffic flow and then having the driver send in his destination
  to a central computer which then checks his location against the
  flow and advises that person on the quickest route.  Of course that
  data will too go in a database to be sold.

- police in many states are trying to receive more revenue by ticketing
  more people for the "crime" of speeding.  They now have automated 
  systems on popular streets and highways that are hooked up to
  cameras and radar detectors.  If you exceed the speed limit, the
  cameras take a picture of your plate and you are mailed a speeding
  ticket.  The greater privacy implications of this are that the
  cameras can run full time and are given de facto toleration in 
  society.  They can also be used to monitor every citizens transportation
  behavior and patterns.

: 1) What level of technology would Ted allow me to have?

I can't speak for Ted, but FC covered that in the Manifesto on paragraphs
207-212.

: Come on Ric give me a guess at how far down the old ladder we been
: fighting our way up for twenty thousand years Ted wish us to go.

It's not a ladder though.  You're thinking linearly and that's too
simplistic.  Everything is interconnected in a very complicated way.
You can't simply isolate one thing, evaluate it, and then move on
to the next.  By itself technology is innocent and imposes nothing 
on freedom.  In combination with other parts of technology and
when it is abused (typical use by companies and government) it 
becomes very harmful to our freedom.  FC's proposal to destroy 
technology is much more complicated that you seem to be understanding
it as it's reached only after accepting that the current encroachment
on our freedom by technology cannot be restricted and will only
increase.  It's an undesirable solution in FC's opinion, but there
appears to be no other way out of the ironic situation that technology
has forced us into.

: In so must as we slave to big business/government are very happy for the
: most part with our lot, how are you and Ted planning on taking Technology
: away from us?

That's the funny part which you're honesty reveals.  Lots of people are
happy with their position as tools and that's what society encourages.
But lots of people are also unhappy and if you start to ask them about
their own goals, their expectations of the future, how little time
they have for things unrelated to the system, you'll find that either
they are damned upset about how constricted their lives are or they
are content to be wage slaves whose lives are consumed by the system 
while they receive little in return.

: Not by reason as Ted first choice was by bombing people. For some reason I
: don't think that any amount of pipe bombs is going to do anything but
: annoy people and getting them to hunt the senders down.

Bombings make people pay attention and can be chaotic enough to make 
people think about the motives of the bomber, though as soon as the
media gets a hold of the story it will be oversimplified and distorted.
The bombings that FC did would not have been meaningful if they
were not accompanied by his various notes of communication.

: So Ted wish to take the place of the people now in power and tell me what
: to do in their place?

Not really.  FC wanted people to have freedom (themselves included) which
means that there would be as few restrictions on people as possible,
replaced with localized responsibility.  Part of the reason that things
today rely so much on the system is that no one takes charge of them
at a local level.  If every local community could take care of its
own problems then we wouldn't need government leaders to control us.
There are some complications with this model, but some communities
have adopted it recently and it seems to have positive results.  At
the very least, it decreases the need for a larger system to intrude
on a local area's lifestyle.  It is still possible that the local
system will intrude as much or more than the previous one.

: Hmm you would need a world wide control of printing presses assuming you
: would allow us to have 15 century technology.

I think FC was pro-communication, but it's not clear to what extent
communication fits their model for revolution because communication
channels can be abused by the system just as well as between two
free humans.

: By the way you would need such complete control over everyone in ever
: corner of the planet, that the only way of doing so would be a very high
: technology indeed!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Or widespread understanding of the dangers of technology.

: How are you planning on taking technology away, how in the hell are you
: going to do that? 

Education and detailing the abuses of technology.  It may also be
possible to force companies and governments to stop all information 
collection on people.  As an intermediate step, I think this is much
more achievable though it will not solve the problem unless it is
absolute.

: Hmm you hope to made civilization collapse, by sending pipe bombs! Hmm
: civilization in the last hundred years have survive two world wars that
: kill 60 million people or so and you and Ted are going to bring it down?

You're stuck on thinking of the deaths rather than the disruption.

: Civilization that survive the black death that kill 1/3 of the
: known human race at the time!

If you are Euro-centric in your thinking, yes it killed 1/3 of the human
race.

: And if you and Ted could cause a completely collapse, beside killing a
: large part of the human race what would you gain?

Freedom from the system, life with more of a meaning than serving as
a tool for the system.

: The part of the world that retain the most technology would just expanse
: and in a few hundred years at the very most we would be right back to now.

Paragraphs 207-212 explain FC's position on this topic.  Jumping to the
end, FC says:

   212. Would society EVENTUALLY develop again toward an
   industrial-technological form? Maybe, but there is no use in worrying
   about it, since we can't predict or control events 500 or 1,000 years
   in the future. Those problems must be dealt with by the people who
   will live at that time.

: Hmm the internet is great! The internet that need to have a very high
: technology to support it is great?
:
: You mean that some technology is good? How can that be?

Communication among we who are discontent and hate the system is good.
As FC writes:

   202. It would be hopeless for revolutionaries to try to attack the
   system without using SOME modern technology. If nothing else they must
   use the communications media to spread their message. But they should
   use modern technology for only ONE purpose: to attack the
   technological system.

: God you have no logic at all do you?

My logic is fine.  You're tripping yourself up on the black and white
interpretation which simply doesn't work.  That's probably why you
can't understand the Manifesto.

: You know Ric my fear is morbid? Well I would like to eliminate serial
: killers from society, that for sure no matter what reason they give for
: thier killings.

What about war leaders that kill thousands of people and ruin the living
conditions of entire countries?  One of the first thing the US did to 
Iraq was to bomb their waste treatment centers, ensuring that the
land would be without hygienic conditions, which is necessary when you
have a large, crowded population.  

What about the factories that kill millions (billions?) of animals
so we can enjoy eating them?

What about all of the abortions that society has decided are better
than having millions of unwanted children?

You haven't answered these questions yet.  Do you have an answer 
do you just pass over the uncomfortable questions?

: I have no great fear of you and your the risk to me or any one by a few
: sociopaths is very small and the threat you pose to our civilization is
: zero. Still it would be nice if we could find a way of finding those type
: of people in their childhood and helping them or at least mading sure
: they don't harm others.

You'd have a society of purely uncreative conformist tools if you  
could stop those who think critically and take ration action.  Is
that what you really want?

: PS one more time , what level of technology would you and Ted allow us to
: have and how would you stop us from rebuilding from whatever level you
: would force us down to?

FC's opinions are included in the Manifesto.  My position is less clear
and is still in development and I tend to think that technology that
increases communication is valuable and that technology that collects
information should be absolutely restricted from that task.  An 
informative campaign that documents the current intrusion into our
freedom and discusses technology under development to do the same
could have a very positive effect.

-Ric
